Scope: packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts + docs/adr/0012-notification-platform.md (§6, §8, §10, §11, §12), docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md (D3), docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md (§3, `credentialRef`), docs/adr/0049-no-unenforced-security-properties.md, packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts (`DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES`, `HANDLER_STATUS_RETIRED`), packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.test.ts (the `toHaveLength(3)` / `not.toContain('/devices')` pin), packages/runtime/src/request-schema-gate.conformance.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts (`actionUrlFor`), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts (`sourceObject` / `sourceId` / `actionUrl`), packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts (the house `credentialRef` members), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts (`LocaleSchema`), packages/spec/src/system/email-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/notification.zod.ts (`NotificationChannelSchema`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`RegisterDeviceRequest` re-export), ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/hooks/useApiDiscovery.ts (the `/devices` body template), the PR's five test files, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts and .changeset/29067-push-device-registry-spec.md

Closed #29101 read for history only. The dispatching seat's own ACCEPT is not an input.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` accept set widens, nothing else moves — right.** Three new optional members (`vendor`, `appId`, `locale`); `token`, `platform`, `deviceId`, `name` are byte-identical in shape. The two refusals the widening adds (`vendor` outside `apns` / `fcm`; `locale` not a BCP 47 tag) sit on new keys no body sent before carries, so every body that parsed on `main` parses here (pinned by `register-device-request.test.ts`). The object stays a non-strict `z.object`, as its siblings in the protocol-method block are, so unknown keys are stripped exactly as before.
2. **`RegisterDeviceResponseSchema`, `UnregisterDeviceRequestSchema`, `UnregisterDeviceResponseSchema`: description only — right.** Shape unchanged; pinned.
3. **Seven new public schemas plus bare aliases, no removal, no rename — right, additive.** `PushRouteSchema` / `PushDeliveryDataSchema` (api), `PushVendorSchema` / `ApnsTransportConfigSchema` / `FcmTransportConfigSchema` / `PushServiceConfigSchema` / `UserDeviceSchema` (system), each with a `z.input` alias and an isomorphic pin (811 → 818, +6 then +1, arithmetic checks against the modules). Both barrels re-export with `export *`; the consumer type-check gates are green, so no name collides. No ADR-0087 tombstone, conversion or semantic entry is owed: no published field is removed or renamed.
4. **`INotificationService` gains four OPTIONAL members — right.** An interface implementers fill: optional members keep every existing implementation valid (pinned by the send-only case in `notification-service.test.ts`); a caller must test for absence, which the docblock states.
5. **`DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` unchanged; Wanted 2 not built — right.** Read in the live tree: `HANDLER_STATUS_RETIRED` rules "an endpoint that has no handler yet is simply not registered"; the table's own comment records the device rows' earlier removal for exactly the declared-not-served defect; and `request-schema-gate.conformance.test.ts` iterates `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` and reds any POST/PUT/PATCH row with a `requestSchema` and no violating-body case, a case that cannot be written until the route answers 400 instead of 404. Adding the rows here would reintroduce the recorded defect and red a runtime gate. The catalog pin (`toHaveLength(3)`, `not.toContain('/devices')`) stays as it is on `main`.
6. **`PushServiceConfigSchema` is exported but not wired into `StackSchema.config` — right.** The card asked for it where email transport selection lives, or why not; the header says why (no reader yet; a key is never authorable before something honours it). The authorable-surface generator enumerates exported object schemas, so the surface baseline grew by the new keys anyway, which is what the changeset's `Metadata-protocol: added` answers to.
7. **`UserDeviceSchema` lives in `system/push-device.zod.ts`, not ADR-0012 §10's `notification/device.zod.ts` — right.** `packages/spec/src/notification/` does not exist on `main`; `system/notification.zod.ts` is the realized home of the notification vocabulary, and `email-config.zod.ts` / `sms-config.zod.ts` sit in `system/`. The narrowing from §6 (vendor pair, three platforms, camelCase, no `.default(true)` on `enabled`) is stated in the header; §6 routes HMS / Xiaomi / OPPO / vivo to alternate channel plugins, so the closed pair is the ADR's own reading.
8. **`PushRouteSchema` admits exactly a same-server relative path — right, and it held against the attempts in this round.** Tried: `//host`, `/\host`, `/` + tab + `/host`, `/` + newline, `javascript:`, `https:`, a relative path, the empty string, a path with `\..\` — all refused by the regex (`^\/(?![/\\])[^\s\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$`); `/opportunity/123?tab=notes#activity` and `/` are admitted. `%5C` is a path byte to a URL parser, not a backslash, so it is correctly admitted. The derivation claim checks against the tree: `actionUrlFor` in `messaging-service.ts` answers `payload.url` / `payload.actionUrl`, else `/{object}/{id}` from the emit's source, else `undefined`, which is the three-way rule the header states. No `notify` key is added.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29067-push-device-registry-spec.md` declares `@objectstack/spec: minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. The diff publishes new exports, a widened request and four optional interface members, and removes nothing: `minor` is the level the diff publishes. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` matches ① items 1–4. `Metadata-protocol: added` matches the authorable-surface growth in ① item 6 and the seat's amended claim (the original server-seat claim's `none` was superseded by the spec-seat claim 6572317452). The PR body carries the same two lines; the `Check Changeset` and PR-body-guard check-runs on this head are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from os-dev-report 6573960254 (head `73fabdf2`; `833e9bd7` adds the `LocaleSchema` commit on the seat's FAIL round) and the PR body:

- **open_questions 1 (route rows here or with handlers): answered A, right** — ① item 5. The seat's claim amendment records the same; Wanted 2 is a declared hand-off to #29068 together with the catalog-pin flip and the runtime gate case.
- **open_questions 2 (new public names): well-formed against house spellings; approval not ruled here.** Schema names end in `Schema` with a bare `z.input` alias (ADR-0122); keys are camelCase; enum values are lowercase data values (`apns`, `fcm`, `sandbox`, `production`); `credentialRef` is the one spelling ADR-0097 §3 / ADR-0143 D3 and every `connector-auth.zod.ts` variant use; `deviceId` / `token` / `platform` / `name` are the published request's own; `teamId` / `keyId` / `topic` / `projectId` are the vendors' own terms in camelCase. `UserDeviceSchema` is ADR-0012 §6's name. Nothing here is malformed; the maintainer's approval is a separate act.
- **open_questions 3 (keep `vendor` and `deviceId` optional): answered A, right** — requiring either would refuse `{ token, platform }`, which parses on `main`, and would contradict the card's own `Clause-②: yes`. The server-minted id and the platform → vendor derivation are stated in the describes and in the service contract.
- **open_questions 4 (user-only ownership; displaced row removed; web names its vendor; disabled rows listed): answered A, acceptable as a contract.** ADR-0012's own scoping concern (Risks §6) is per environment, not per organization, and `messaging-service.ts` writes `organization_id` on the notification, so "the organization travels on the notification" is the tree's existing posture. Removing the displaced row is consistent with "one live owner per token" and with the card's "moves to that user". The web-vendor sentence is where the two faces of the contract disagree — ④ should-fix 1.
- **Deviation: authorable-surface system shard restored from `main` and regenerated** — a generated artifact outside ④'s scope; `check:generated` is inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates` leg.
- **Deviation: Wanted 7 (`NotificationChannelSchema` JSDoc) rides the server slice** — right; the JSDoc's "push has no delivery implementation" is still true on this head.
- **`Skills-docs: none`** — right for a declared-ahead face with no served route and no read key; the server slice that serves them owns the docs.
- **Out-of-scope finding (the `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` JSDoc is false on `main`)** — left byte-identical, carried to #29068. Right: correcting it here would be a hunk in a file the claim did not need.
- **Escalated, not in the dev's list:** `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/hooks/useApiDiscovery.ts` carries a `POST /devices` body template `{ token: '', platform: 'web' }`. Under this contract a `web` registration without `vendor` is refused by the server, so when #29068 mounts the route that template needs `vendor`. Not a `hits` file and not a finding on this PR; named here so #29068 / #29042 pick it up.

Nothing is escalated to the maintainer beyond the name approval the PR already requests.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer (#29068 the device registry, #29041 the push channel). No must-fix. Six should-fix items, none of which changes the verdict.

**packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/index.ts** — barrel lines only. Import graph checked: `api/protocol` → `system/push-config` and `system/translation`; `system/push-device` → `system/push-config`, `system/translation`; `contracts/notification-service` → type-only imports of `api/protocol` and `system/push-device`. No cycle; `api` importing `system` has precedent in the same file (`ServedTranslationDataSchema`). Holds.

**packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts** — the widening holds (① item 1). Two findings on what the describes promise:

- **should-fix 1 — the two faces of the web-vendor rule disagree.** The `vendor` describe says "web has no core vendor, so a web registration names fcm or is refused"; `INotificationService.registerDevice` says "A `web` registration names its vendor", and the enum admits `apns` on `web` (Safari web push is delivered through APNs). A Console built to the service contract sends `vendor: 'apns', platform: 'web'`; a server built to the describe refuses it. One sentence, in both places, before #29068 serves the route: either "names its vendor" or "names fcm", not one each.
- **should-fix 2 — the web-without-vendor refusal is prose, not schema.** The describe promises a refusal the schema does not perform; today it falls to the handler, so the request-schema gate at the route will not see it. The `[PLANNED — not yet served]` marker covers the gap on this head, and expressing it now as a refinement would refuse `{ token, platform: 'web' }`, which parses on `main` (a narrowing of an unserved body). So the cure is #29068's: the handler refuses it as `VALIDATION_FAILED` and adds that body to the request-schema gate's violating-body case, or the schema gains the refinement in the same PR under its own declaration. Either way the first consumer must own it; naming it in the hand-off list is what is missing here.

**packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts** — holds (① item 8). The route is derived from the one value the inbox already serves, so no authorable key is added and the `notify` node's `actionUrl` (any string, including an absolute URL) is dropped at the push rather than failing the delivery, as the header states. `PushRouteSchema` is a plain `z.string()` rather than a `lazySchema`, as `PushVendorSchema` is; the pin test and the generators accept both, so this is a style note, not a finding.

**packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts** — the four members hold against ADR-0012 §6 / §12 (register-or-refresh, one live owner, invalidate on `BadDeviceToken` / `Unregistered` / `UNREGISTERED`, disabled rows kept). Importing `z.input` types from the zod modules has precedent (`analytics-service.ts`, `approval-service.ts`).

- **should-fix 3 — `unregisterDevice`'s not-found mechanism is implicit.** The docblock says a foreign or unknown `deviceId` "answers not found (`NOT_FOUND`, 404 at the device route), never a success", but the return type is `UnregisterDeviceResponse` = `{ success: boolean }`, so the only way to honour the sentence is to throw; the toy registry in the test throws an `Error` with `code: 'NOT_FOUND'`, the contract text does not say so, and `success` becomes a member that is always `true`. State the mechanism (throw an error carrying `code: 'NOT_FOUND'`, as the test does and as the dispatcher's error exit maps) so #29068 and the test agree with the contract rather than with each other.

**packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts** — holds against ADR-0143 D3: both secrets are `credentialRef` members, the inline spellings an operator would reach for are refused by name with `credentialRef` as the prescription, `keyRef` / `serviceAccountRef` / `bundleId` are aliases, all three blocks are `strictObject` with the house "strict from birth" history, and the near-miss and content refusals are pinned.
